findings.evidence: Line 453-454 is the whole proof; the docstring at 444-445 concedes "`mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule` and `isRestricted_pi_iff` already carry the left-hand side to the same normal form". The simpNF output quoted in the author's reply confirms it mechanically: `Left-hand side simplifies ... using simp only [@TauCeti.Huber.mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule, @TauCeti.Huber.isRestricted_pi_iff]`.
findings.fix: Delete `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule_pi_iff` (lines 442-454) and drop it from the module docstring line 34-35, leaving `isRestricted_pi_iff` as the single componentwise lemma. A submodule-level consumer writes `simp [mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule]` (or plain `simp`, since both components are tagged).
findings.issue: `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule_pi_iff` duplicates the composition of two existing `@[simp]` lemmas: `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule` (line 437, `Iff.rfl`) and the new `isRestricted_pi_iff` (line 172). Its proof is literally `simp only [mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule]; exact isRestricted_pi_iff`, and its LHS is not in simp normal form, so it can never fire in a simp set — every consumer reaches the RHS by `simp` through the two lemmas already present.

summary: `isRestricted_pi_iff` is new and correctly delegates to Mathlib's `tendsto_pi_nhds`, but `mem_restrictedMvPowerSeriesSubmodule_pi_iff` is a composite that its two component `@[simp]` lemmas already prove, by the author's own simpNF evidence.
